top_choice_rationale: P002 (Helpman and Melitz) rests on a mature, general framework for exporter selection and reallocation across firms. It has been tested directly on firm-level and transaction-level data in many countries for over twenty years, which is stronger confirmation than the indirectly identified collateral channel in P001. Attribution is the main weakness: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are uncredited, and Helpman's marginal credit has to be separated from the 2008 prize and from his protection-for-sale work. I judge these manageable with a citation limited to the theoretical integration of firm heterogeneity and selection, with no claim on the exporter-premium facts or the Eaton-Kortum strand. P001 is a very close second, with a cleaner two-author origin and nearly three decades of use as a building block. I would not oppose it if its citation names only the collateral-price feedback. P003 is serious and well scrutinised, but its credit spans two strands and the three-name cap leaves out Dorn and parts of the task framework. Any of the three awards is better than P000, because each recognises a mature, well-scrutinised achievement. This rests on general knowledge and the supplied committee text, not on independent verification, and I do not treat support counts as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: No tie to Helpman, Melitz, Kiyotaki, Moore, Autor, Hanson or Katz is apparent from the profile. My field (pricing, exchange-rate pass-through, trade) is adjacent to P002, which may incline me toward it. I have co-authored with the chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026); Hassler prefers P001, and I weighed his arguments on their merits. I am married to Magdalena Andersson, a public fact with no evident bearing on this ballot. Conflicts are disclosed, not adjudicated.
